name: capture-anchored-pacing
title: Anchor thread C's capture pacing to when the display presented (E phase 2, in process on Windows and Mac) and add the capture seams later PRs use
protocol_changes: None on the desktop wire (ALPN stays pb-mapper/desktop/2) and none on the helper pipe: HELPER_PROTOCOL and the .v10 pipe names stay, RemoteBackend reports no present stamp until helper-push adds one. Public SDK, semver-minor: provided Backend methods submitted_picture, capture_poll and video_paused, and the Presented type.
design:
Why. Thread C's pacer (pacer.rs) lays ticks on an even grid unrelated to when the display presents. When the pace equals the present rate (Balanced 60 on a 60 Hz panel, Smooth 120 on 120 Hz, a ProMotion Mac) a picture waits up to a period for the next tick (model: mean 5.8-7.2 ms at 60 Hz and 2.9 ms at 120 Hz, falling to about 1 ms) and the grid drops one present per drift cycle, a visible hitch. airhand anchors its timeline on the present: client/src-tauri/src/host/pace.rs:34-50 (an early window of P/4, creep of at most P/64), stamps from host/capture/dxgi.rs:677-679 converted by host/clock.rs:42-76. This PR does it in process on both hosts (the helper path follows in helper-push) and adds every thread C seam the later PRs need, so none of them re-touches the five #[deny(clippy::missing_trait_methods)] impls.

1. Pacer (pacer.rs). Add `anchored: bool`. `earliest()` = if anchored { max(next - P/4, last + 3P/4) } else { next }. `consume(now, presented: Option<Instant>)`: None keeps today's rule byte for byte and clears `anchored`; a stamp later than now is clamped to now; a stamp older than one period counts as None; Some(at): base = if at >= next - P/4 { max(at, next - P/64) } else { next }; next = base + P; anchored = true. Keep the 3/4-period floor after a stall, ticks skipped only for backpressure, and the long-run bound of pace x 64/63. set_pace is unchanged.

2. Seams. All are provided methods whose defaults keep today's behaviour, each forwarded in Box (backend.rs:228), PlatformBackend and NativeBackend (native.rs:114 and 422), RemoteBackend (oop/client.rs:237) and examples/input_acceptance/guarded.rs:35.
- `pub struct Presented { pub at: Instant, pub presents: u32 }` (Copy, #[non_exhaustive], exported with the other backend types) and `Backend::submitted_picture(&self) -> Option<Presented>`: the present time of the picture the last capture_video submitted and how many presents it covered (1 = none skipped). None for liveness and keyframe repeats and for undated pictures. RemoteBackend returns None.
- `Backend::capture_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { self.drain_poll() }`: how often thread C re-polls an armed pull capture. capture_poll_after and the input hot-poll path (worker/capture.rs ~143-176) use it instead of drain_poll, so a source can push encoder output while its capture is still polled (win-mf-output-events relies on this).
- `Backend::video_paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`: thread C calls it with true on the transition into the all-paused branch (worker/capture.rs ~236) and with false on the way out, before the resume capture. RemoteBackend implements an explicit no-op (DXGI is pull and runs nothing while paused; no helper message). mac-capture-cadence implements it.
- VideoSource (platform/mod.rs): `fn presented(&self) -> Option<Presented> { None }`; `fn drain_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { Self::DRAIN }`; `const CAPTURE_POLL: Option<Duration> = Self::DRAIN;` with `fn capture_poll(&self) -> Option<Duration> { Self::CAPTURE_POLL }` (instance methods so one encoder instance can fall back to polling); `fn paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`; `fn retune(&mut self, display: &Display, limits: VideoLimits) -> Result<bool> { Ok(false) }`. PlatformBackend forwards each to the open source and uses the consts when none is open.
- configure_video (native.rs:151-156): validate the limits; if a source is open and `retune(&context.display, limits)` returns Ok(true), keep it, otherwise drop it as today; store the limits either way. A context change still rebuilds through capture_video's context compare (native.rs:191-206). Thread C still sets keyframe on a limits change.
- platform/synthetic.rs: SynVideo implements retune (true for an fps-only change, false for a size change) and gains a dated push mode (pictures stamped at a configurable rate and drift, waking its Waker) for the tests.

3. Thread C (worker/capture.rs, worker.rs; static dispatch only, Engine<B: Backend>). capture_at() uses pacer.earliest(). The submit path calls consume(now, backend.submitted_picture().map(|p| p.at)); the backpressure and skip paths pass None. The helper drain long-poll bound (HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX at worker/capture.rs:366) uses capture_at() instead of pacer.next().

4. macOS (platform/macos/capture.rs, video.rs). In the ScreenCaptureKit output callback, under the existing Latest lock (capture.rs:138-144), store `arrived = Instant::now()` and count Complete pictures, Idle samples and pictures replaced before a take in capture::Shared (no allocation). take() returns, for a fresh picture, its arrival and the number of Complete pictures since the last take; MacVideo::presented returns them for a fresh submit and None for repeats. SCStreamFrameInfoDisplayTime feeds diagnostics only, converted by its age against mach_absolute_time with the cached timebase (airhand host/clock.rs:29-40); no CMSync feature.

5. Windows in process (platform/windows/video/mod.rs and mod.rs; add Win32_System_Performance to the windows crate features). Convert LastPresentTime by its age: QueryPerformanceCounter now minus the stamp, with QueryPerformanceFrequency cached in a OnceLock; a negative age (read-order race) counts as 0, an age over 1 s gives None; result Instant::now() - age (std's Instant is QPC-based on Windows, so this is exact up to read skew). Keep `latest_at` and the summed AccumulatedFrames beside latest_pending; a picture left pending by Full or an empty allocator keeps its old stamp and consume ignores it once it is older than a period. Fresh pictures use the present Instant, kept strictly increasing, for pts_us and the sample duration; repeats use now. Statistics and video_bench gain `coalesced_presents` (sum of AccumulatedFrames - 1 over fresh acquires). First frame (R3-first-frame; airhand host/capture/dxgi.rs:632-633): in acquire (video/mod.rs ~571-618), when `latest` is None and the resource is present, copy it as a new image whatever LastPresentTime says, leave it undated, and log once per encoder at debug the first acquire's LastPresentTime and AccumulatedFrames. video_bench mirrors the new pacer and prints present-to-submit p50/p95.

6. Diagnostics. A once-a-second debug event `desktop_capture_pacing` from worker/window.rs roll(): present-to-submit wait p50/p95 (submit Instant - Presented.at), dated share of submits, captures/s, presents/s, coalesced presents/s (sum of presents - 1), empty polls/s. Fixed buffers, no allocation per frame.

7. Docs. Reword rule 2 of 'Video pipeline and performance model' (docs/remote-desktop.md ~1218-1222) and the host capture paragraphs, keeping its sub-rules (skips only for backpressure, the long-run rate, the 3/4-period floor, creep of at most P/64); the constants table; the new Backend methods. No model figures in docs; the CHANGELOG bullet says what changes and gains figures only from the device runs.
verification:
Here (this Mac): `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`, then `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`.
New tests: pacer: dated sources at 59.94, 60, 60.05, 120 and 120.05 Hz are taken within 1 ms of their stamp with no present skipped; 144 and 165 Hz at pace 60 and 120 stay within +-2% and never exceed pace x 64/63; undated consumes reproduce today's grid exactly; a future stamp is clamped; after a stall the 3/4-period floor holds. Worker (Manual clock, dated SynVideo at 60.05 Hz and at 60 Hz + 100 ppm): zero wait and no replaced pictures; a push source presenting 1 ms before the tick is taken on arrival; pacing_is_even_and_skips_ticks_without_bursts and all existing pacing and IDR tests stay green; video_paused fires exactly once per transition and not when one of two viewers pauses; retune keeps the source on an fps-only change and rebuilds on a size change.
CI rust-windows-desktop (windows-latest): `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-features`, including a QPC-to-Instant unit test (now maps within 1 ms, an older count maps earlier, a future count maps to now, a count over 1 s old maps to None). CI rust-macos-desktop. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux (change under crates/): `cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping` then `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`.
measurement:
Zero cost on the data path: `RUST_LOG=off cargo run --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --example host_send_bench`, 3 runs at master (1515eda) and 3 at the branch; allocations per frame must stay at about 19.1 / 59.1 / 167.4 (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-desktop-pipeline/README.md).
Device, release builds, master against the branch: Windows host in process on a 60 Hz mode, a 59.94 Hz mode and 120 Hz (pace 60 and 120; scrolling and a 120 fps animation): `cargo run --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --example video_bench -- 30 60 --animate` present-to-submit p50/p95 and coalesced_presents per 30 s, plus a live session's desktop_capture_pacing; capture fps must be unchanged or higher. Mac host with Screen Recording granted: `target/release/examples/deployed APP_CONFIG_PATH OUT/<arm>-<n> selftest 40 --tcp --feedback-log --fps 60` and `--fps 120 --quality smooth --fps-override`, order A B B A: desktop_capture_pacing wait p50/p95 and presents per capture; presented FPS must not fall; typing echo must not regress. Record everything under docs/benchmarks/<date>-capture-pacing/ with GPU, driver, display mode and OS build, indexed in docs/README.md.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac: the pacer, the seams, the worker and the synthetic dated source, and host_send_bench. The Windows QPC conversion and acquire changes compile and test only in CI. The effect (shorter present-to-capture wait, no dropped present) is device-only: Windows hardware, and a Mac host needs a Screen Recording grant this session does not have.

name: win-keep-awake
title: Windows host: keep the display and the system awake while a viewer session captures, and wake a dark display when it starts
protocol_changes: None: the helper worker runs the same video source, so no helper request is needed and HELPER_PROTOCOL is unchanged.
design:
Why. A view-only viewer's picture freezes when the host's display-off timeout fires (often 5-15 minutes; DXGI gets no new pictures), a Modern Standby laptop sleeps mid-session and kills it, and a controller who only moves the pointer neither resets the idle timer nor wakes the display (SetCursorPos is not input). The Mac host already holds an NSActivity with IdleDisplaySleepDisabled (platform/macos/timer.rs:28-40).

Design (kept inside platform/windows, so it needs neither oop/server.rs nor timer.rs):
1. New platform/windows/power.rs: a process-wide keeper driven by `touch()`, an atomic store of the time (no allocation, safe on the data path). The Windows VideoSource's submit (platform/windows/mod.rs, VideoSource::submit) calls power::touch() on every call, in process and in the helper worker alike, so it runs exactly while a session captures.
2. The first touch starts one watchdog thread that parks on a condvar while idle (no wake-ups when nothing shares). On the first touch after at least 2 s without one, it calls PowerCreateRequest (simple reason string) and PowerSetRequest for PowerRequestDisplayRequired and PowerRequestSystemRequired, and SetThreadExecutionState(ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED) once to turn a dark display on, so a session that starts or resumes with the display off gets its first picture without local input. While touches keep coming (checked each 1 s) it holds. 2 s after the last touch (pause, close, pipe loss, worker exit) it calls PowerClearRequest for both, CloseHandle, and parks. Drop and process exit release.
3. Log acquire and release once each at debug.
4. Add the needed windows crate features (Win32_System_Power, Win32_System_Threading).
5. Docs: Windows hosting paragraph, the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) where display sleep is mentioned; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (nothing changes off Windows). CI rust-windows-desktop: `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-features` including a test of the keeper's state machine with an injected clock. CI nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: Windows device: set the display-off timeout to 1 min; a view-only viewer on a changing screen for 3 min, before (the picture freezes, received_fps falls to 0) and after (it keeps updating); `powercfg /requests` lists DISPLAY and SYSTEM entries while capturing, none after disconnect and none 2-3 s into a pause; turn the display off (or let it time out), then connect or resume: the first picture arrives without local input. Repeat through the installed background helper. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: CI build and test only; the effect is device-only.

name: helper-pipe-transfer
title: Windows helper: move units in large pipe reads (mio 1.2.5, one vectored write per record, larger relay buffers and pipe quotas)
protocol_changes: None: the records on the pipe stay byte-identical; only how they are written and read changes. HELPER_PROTOCOL unchanged.
design:
Why. Units cross two named pipes (worker -> service -> app). Each record goes out as four writes (oop/server.rs:62-65, client.rs:110-112), the service relays with default 8 KiB copies, and mio 1.2.4 reads named pipes in small chunks, so an IDR takes many IOCP completions per hop: about 0.5-1 ms per IDR across the two hops, 0.1-0.3 ms per 20-50 KB P-frame, more for 4K Quality units of 100-300 KB.

1. `cargo update -p mio --precise 1.2.5` (lockfile only; tokio 1.49 accepts it).
2. ipc.rs gains `write_record` that sends the JSON record and the byte record as one vectored write, looping on partial writes with IoSlice::advance_slices; server.rs:62-65 and client.rs:110-112 use it.
3. helper/service.rs:237 uses `tokio::io::copy_bidirectional_with_sizes` with 64 KiB each way (256 KiB is harmless).
4. helper/pipe.rs: in and out quotas of 64-256 KiB, so a worker's write completes without waiting on the reader; 1 MiB only if the micro-bench shows a gain.
5. New Windows-only example examples/pipe_relay_bench.rs relaying 20 KB, 170 KB, 1 MB and 3.7 MB records through two named pipes, service-style.
6. Docs: the helper transport paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet only with measured numbers.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features` after the lockfile change (named pipes are Windows-only; this checks the rest builds); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. CI rust-windows-desktop: `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-features` (a write_record round trip with partial writes). CI nat-traversal.yml (Cargo.lock changed).
measurement: Windows device, release: `cargo run --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --example pipe_relay_bench` comparing mio 1.2.4 against 1.2.5 and four writes against one vectored write: time per record and completions; the worker-to-host delay of real IDRs through the helper before and after. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: Build and the non-Windows test suite here; named pipes and every effect are CI/device-only.

name: native-cursor
title: Desktop viewers: show host pointer shapes as native OS cursors and switch them without waiting for a Flutter frame
protocol_changes: None on the wire, Rust or FFI. A new runner method channel `pb_mapper/desktop_pointer` (cursor_create, cursor_set, cursor_delete) on all three desktop runners, with its Dart client and test fake.
design:
Why. A controlling desktop viewer over a custom or upArrow shape hides the OS pointer and has Flutter paint the bitmap at the last hover position, so that pointer trails the hand by Flutter's event-to-present pipeline, about 1.5-3 refreshes (25-50 ms at 60 Hz) and feels floaty next to the hardware cursor shown over named shapes. It happens often: Mac hosts name only 7 standard cursors (platform/macos/cursor.rs:134-142), so open or closed hand, context menu, drag-copy and the window-corner resizes are custom; Windows hosts name 14 shared handles (platform/windows/cursor.rs:20-35), so every cursor an app loads itself (browser grab, Office, Adobe, CAD) is custom. A Mac viewer also lacks system cursors for busy, move and diagonal resizes from Windows hosts. A shape change today waits for a MouseRegion rebuild and the post-frame MouseTracker pass. airhand scales host cursors to the picture (client/src/lib/session.ts:802-821).

1. A new channel `pb_mapper/desktop_pointer` in new runner files, so the desktop_video runners stay untouched (viewer-scroll and relative-pointer add their methods to the same files): `cursor_create {id, rgba (straight alpha), width, height, hot_x, hot_y}` (physical pixels after Dart's scaling), `cursor_set {id}`, `cursor_delete {id}`. Do not use the engine's own Windows cursor methods.
2. Windows (ui/windows/runner/desktop_pointer.{h,cpp}, constructed in flutter_window.cpp like DesktopIme): CreateIconIndirect from a 32-bpp top-down DIB section (BGRA) and a 1-bpp mask derived from alpha; DestroyIcon on delete; ::SetCursor on the platform thread. The engine's WM_SETCURSOR returns TRUE for HTCLIENT without setting a cursor (flutter_window.cc:725-731), so the runner's cursor stays until Dart activates a system cursor, which MouseTracker does on enter and exit.
3. macOS (ui/darwin/DesktopPointer.swift under #if os(macOS), registered in ui/macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift and added to the macOS Runner target in project.pbxproj): NSCursor(image:hotSpot:) from an NSImage holding an NSBitmapImageRep at pixel size, size and hotspot in points (pixels / backingScaleFactor); set(). If the FlutterView responds to `didUpdateMouseCursor:`, call it with the cursor so the engine's cursorUpdate: restores ours; otherwise re-set it from a cursorUpdate local monitor.
4. Linux (ui/linux/runner/desktop_pointer.{h,cc}, registered in my_application.cc): gdk_cursor_new_from_surface (a cairo image surface with the device scale) and gdk_window_set_cursor on the FlView's window, the one the engine uses (fl_view.cc:158-166).
5. Dart: new ui/lib/src/ffi/desktop_pointer.dart client (and test fake). In remote_cursor_layer.dart add `RemoteShapeCursor extends MouseCursor`; RemotePointerRegion passes one constant instance while mouse && controlling. Its session listens to RemotePointer, DesktopCursor.shape and the viewport scale and calls the platform directly on activate and every change, with no rebuild. Kinds the viewer OS has go through SystemChannels.mouseCursor activateSystemCursor (mapping per viewer platform; on macOS wait, progress, help, move and both diagonal resizes take the bitmap path). Kinds it lacks, plus upArrow and custom, take the bitmap path: scale by picture scale x devicePixelRatio, clamped to 0.35-2 and at most 128 logical px; cache per (content, scale within 2%), at most 16 like _shapeCache; cursor_delete on eviction, at session end and on dispose. When not atLocalPointer, as today.
6. Painting stays for viewers that do not control, for touch, and as the fallback when a channel call throws.
7. Docs: the viewer pointer section; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (l10n_untranslated.json stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (widget tests with mocked mouseCursor and desktop_pointer channels, target platform overridden per OS: a shape change issues create+set with no widget rebuild; a macOS target sends 'wait' to the bitmap path; eviction deletes; updated RemotePointerLook tests); icons from AppIcons only; Flutter here is 3.50 (CI 3.44.9), discard files 3.50 rewrites. macOS app: `bash scripts/build/pb-mapper-ffi-macos.sh`, then in ui/ `FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS=$(uname -m) FLUTTER_XCODE_ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES bash ../scripts/build/flutter-macos.sh build macos --debug`. CI: macos-app, ios-app (the iOS target must not include the macOS-only file or must compile it out), linux-app (`flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software`); the Windows runner compiles only via release-ui.yml with windows_verify_only.
measurement: On this Mac, no Screen Recording needed: `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_ui_host -- --clip clip.h264 --dir target/desktop-ui` (its pointer bands include resize-nwse and a custom checkered disc; add a 'wait' band), connect the macOS app, take control and sweep the bands. (a) Shape-change latency: the host_shape log line against an os_signpost/log from the runner (after) or the engine's activateSystemCursor/MouseTracker path (before), same clock: expect at least one frame less. (b) Painted-pointer latency before: SchedulerBinding.addTimingsCallback paired with PointerEvent.timeStamp (event to rasterFinish plus one refresh); after, no Flutter frame is in the pointer path; confirm with a 240 fps phone video over the custom band. (c) A Mac viewer over the 'wait' band shows the host bitmap, not an arrow. Device: Windows and Linux viewers, 240 fps video of a sweep over a Mac host's open-hand cursor before and after; on Windows GetGuiResources(GR_USEROBJECTS) stays flat across 200 shape changes. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac (Dart tests, the macOS viewer against desktop_ui_host); the Windows and Linux runners build only in CI and their effect is device-only.

name: win-sendinput-moves
title: Windows host: inject pointer moves with absolute SendInput instead of SetCursorPos
protocol_changes: None (Input::Move unchanged; helper requests and responses unchanged).
design:
Why. SetCursorPos is not input: WH_MOUSE_LL hooks and raw-input readers see nothing, GetLastInputInfo never advances (presence and inactivity-lock policies, which power requests do not stop, think nobody is there), a dark display does not wake on a remote move, and a remote drawing gets one point per app message pump instead of the full 250 Hz stream. Latency stays one syscall.

1. WinInput::pointer (platform/windows/input.rs:53-58) sends one INPUT_MOUSE with MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE | MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE | MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK, plus MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE_NOCOALESCE while any button is held (track it in WinInput from button()); coordinates normalized to 0..65535 from SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN read in the thread's per-monitor-aware DPI context and cached until a display change; dwExtraInfo = enigo.get_marker_value(), as send_physical already does.
2. Move the pure Pointer settle logic (platform/macos/pointer.rs:26-50) to the neutral input/cursor.rs, keep macos/pointer.rs's Shared type using it, and use it in WinCursor::read (platform/windows/cursor.rs:50-60): the injected pixel is reported until GetCursorInfo shows it or 250 ms pass, so CursorEcho and the helper's per-Input cursor answer (oop/server.rs:118-121) still see the controller's own echo (SendInput applies asynchronously).
3. UIPI and desktop-switch fallback: if a settle window ends without the pointer reaching the target, use SetCursorPos for moves until the foreground window changes. Log the integrity level with the existing token diagnostics.
4. The helper runs the same injector unchanged.
5. Docs: Windows input paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (the shared settle tests run on every platform; macOS behaviour unchanged). CI rust-windows-desktop: `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-features` with a normalization round trip over every pixel of 1920-, 3840- and 7680-wide virtual desktops with negative origins. CI nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: Windows device: re-run the installed input acceptance of docs/validation/desktop-925-installed-input.json: move_roundtrip and the 30 and 60 Hz movement means must stay about 3.1-3.4 ms (p95 <= 5.1 ms); a RegisterRawInputDevices fixture counts WM_INPUT during remote moves (0 before, > 0 after); GetLastInputInfo advances on a move-only session after, not before; a Tk fixture sleeping 15 ms per message counts WM_MOUSEMOVE during a 1 s remote drag at 250 Hz (about 60 before, about 250 after); with a monitor left of the primary, an absolute move lands on its exact pixel; with an elevated window in front, an in-process host's moves still arrive (fallback). Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: Shared settle logic tested here; Windows code CI-only; effect device-only.

name: viewer-pixel-snap
title: Desktop viewers: keep a 1:1 picture on the device-pixel grid and show a near-1 fit at exactly 1:1
design:
Why. Original-size mode sets exactly one remote pixel per physical pixel (remote_viewport.dart:280-286), but autoScrollTo (227-252) and the fitted centring (fittedRect, 73-83) produce fractional offsets, and the scene is placed by a Transform with that translation (remote_surface.dart:260-273). The texture is sampled bilinearly, so at a half-pixel offset a 1-pixel text stroke becomes two half-intensity pixels, and in original-size mode text alternates between sharp and blurred on every pointer move; the same happens at a fitted 1:1 whose centring falls between pixels (Windows at 125% or 150%). airhand shows a picture up to 4% smaller than its area at 1:1, aligned to device pixels (client/src/lib/fit.ts:1-6, 14, 55-61; docs/architecture.md:213). This is display-side only, not J (encoding the window's size), which stays rejected.

1. RemoteViewport learns the stage's global origin in physical pixels: _ViewportSync or RemoteSurface's LayoutBuilder reads localToGlobal(Offset.zero) after layout and passes it with devicePixelRatio.
2. Snap: whenever the effective scale is 1:1 (original mode, or abs(scene.width x scale x dpr - remotePixels.width) < 0.5), _set snaps the offset so (origin + offset) x dpr is an integer: offset = round((origin + offset) x dpr) / dpr - origin. This covers autoScrollTo, relayout and pinch end, never an active pinch.
3. Near-1 fit: in fit mode, when the fit scale in device pixels s = min(roomPx.w / remote.w, roomPx.h / remote.h) is in [1, 1.04), use exactly 1:1, centred and snapped.
4. toNormalized and toLocal already use the same offset and scale, so input mapping stays exact. Native presenters (mac-viewer-layer, linux-video-plane) follow Flutter's transform, so they inherit the snap.
5. CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (untranslated stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test`: (origin + offset) x dpr is integral after autoScrollTo at random pointer positions, odd stage sizes, dpr 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2 and a fractional stage origin; the near-1 fit gives one device pixel per remote pixel; input round trips. Flutter 3.50 here (CI 3.44.9). CI flutter-syntax-check.
measurement: On this Mac: replay a 1920x1080 text clip through `cargo run --release -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_ui_host -- --clip text.h264 --dir target/desktop-ui` in original-size mode in a window smaller than the picture; Screenshot.app crops of one text line while moving the pointer, before and after: the contrast across a 1-pixel stroke (max minus min) stays at the source's instead of dropping about half at half-pixel offsets. Device: Windows at 125% and 150% scaling, and Linux.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac (unit tests and the visual check); Windows fractional scaling and Linux are device-only.

name: rate-model-latch
title: Latch the Timestamp rate model from per-tick integrated bits within about 2 s
design:
Why. The latch needs two consecutive 3 s windows at pace <= 0.75 x nominal (qos.rs:667-688), so a per-second encoder (AMD or Intel MFTs if they budget per second, SDK backends) overspends nominal/pace times for 6 s or more after every pace drop, and a mid-window bpf cut can latch a per-frame encoder falsely, which receipt-driven rate control would trigger often.

1. qos.rs: tick() diffs ProducedSnapshot every 250 ms into 8 fixed buckets (a sliding 2 s span). Each bucket holds frames, unique frames, non-IDR bits, integrated expected bits (bpf at that tick x the non-IDR frames of that tick) and a paced-low flag.
2. Latch Timestamp when the 2 s span has at least 6 unique frames, every bucket was paced at or below 0.75 x nominal, and non-IDR bits > max(1.3, 0.6 x nominal / mean pace) x the integrated expected bits. The second term stops a per-frame encoder at its content floor from latching (NVIDIA measured up to 1.79 at pace 5 with nominal 120, remote-desktop.md:1586-1592); a per-second encoder overshoots by about nominal/pace and still latches.
3. close_window keeps only the bpf step; the latch stays one-way and keeps its trace.
4. slow_link.rs: Sizes::PerSecond, bytes = bitrate x (now - previous capture) / 8 with the gap capped at 1 s, modelling a per-second encoder including its burst after idle.
5. Docs: the rate-model paragraph and constants.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib qos::` (mid-window bpf cuts never latch a per-frame encoder; a per-second encoder latches within 2.5 s; a fixed-size content-floor encoder at pace 5 never latches) and `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: Release, 3 runs each, before and after: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 slow_link` with slow_presenter_is_capped_by_fps_cap_not_host_backpressure and the bandwidth case run on Sizes::PerSecond: time to rate_model=Timestamp in the trace and sent bitrate / expected (before at least 6 s and up to nominal/pace; after at most 2.5 s); with the default per-frame encoder every existing case shows no latch. Device: `video_bench --pace 60,30,15,5` on an AMD or Intel host to see whether any MFT needs the latch. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: Measure-on-this-Mac (unit tests and slow_link with synthetic encoders); vendor behaviour device-only.

name: viewer-decoder-stats
title: Decoder stats parity: decode time, decoder CPU, hardware and the window's refresh on the Mac; surface-consume time and refresh on Linux; decode or convert time in the quality panel
design:
Why. The Mac viewer reports no decode time, CPU or hardware flag, and the Linux runner reports no timings, so the native presenters (mac-viewer-layer, linux-video-plane) and GPU conversion (linux-gpu-convert) cannot be verified in the field or in acceptance reports. The Windows runner already reports {samples, mean_ms, max_ms} timings (convert, surface_consume) and refreshHz.

1. Swift (DesktopVideo.swift), while timings are on: time VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrame as `timings.decode` (IDRs included); after each unit the feed thread stores clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID), reported as `decoderCpuMs` since attach; always report `hardware` from VideoDecoder.hardware. `refreshHz` becomes the FlutterView window's screen maximumFramesPerSecond, falling back to the fastest screen (moved here from R6-follow-window-refresh).
2. Linux runner (desktop_video.cc): `stats` honours `timings` like Windows: `timings.surface_consume` (frame_ready to acquire) as {samples, mean_ms, max_ms}, and `refreshHz` (DisplayMaxHz). Decode timing needs the module ABI and comes with linux-gpu-convert.
3. Dart: DesktopDecoderStats gains decodeMs = meanMs('decode'), presentMs = meanMs('present') (filled by mac-viewer-layer), convertMs = meanMs('convert') (Windows), decoderCpuMsPerSecond = rate('decoderCpuMs') and hardware. quality_panel.dart shows a row only for what is present, with separate labels for decode (Mac) and convert (Windows); new l10n strings in both locales. The acceptance tool already records `native` as is (ui/tool/desktop_viewer_acceptance.dart:491-505).
4. Docs: the quality panel (docs/remote-desktop.md:1946-1956) and the macOS and Linux decoder sections.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (l10n_untranslated.json stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (DesktopDecoderStats.between with decode, present, convert and decoderCpuMs; panel rows shown only when present); icons from AppIcons. macOS app: `bash scripts/build/pb-mapper-ffi-macos.sh`, then in ui/ `FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS=$(uname -m) FLUTTER_XCODE_ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES bash ../scripts/build/flutter-macos.sh build macos --debug`. CI macos-app, ios-app, linux-app (`flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software`), flutter-syntax-check.
measurement: No speed change. On this Mac: the acceptance viewer's report (scripts/test/desktop-ui-acceptance.md:114-131 with desktop_ui_host) shows native.timings.decode within the harness's paced range for the same clip size and codec (about 2-6 ms BGRA at 1080p-4K) and decoderCpuMs per second; two clock reads per frame only while the panel is open.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac (Dart, macOS app); Linux runner CI-build only.

name: viewer-fps-cap
title: Viewer: remember the decoder's capacity in the fps cap, raise in steps scaled to the ceiling, and drain an age backlog instead of freezing until the IDR
protocol_changes: None (no protocol, FFI or runner change; fixed rings, no allocation per unit).
design:
Why. (a) A consumer slower than the host (Linux software decode, Windows software MF in VMs, 4K120 on weak iGPUs) overshoots about every 5-6 s; most overshoots end in an age drop, a frozen picture until an IDR arrives and an IDR bandwidth spike; slow_presenter's mean pace is 12.4 for a 14.9 fps consumer. (b) At a 120 ceiling a transient backlog that halves the cap to 60 takes about 14 s to clear (CAP_STEP 5 per second after a 3 s hold). (c) On an age backlog the sink drops the queue at push (sink.rs:399-402) and take (599-601) as soon as the head is 250 ms old with 3 queued, sets wait_key and discards every later P-frame, so a consumer whose thread stalled 300 ms then returned shows nothing until the IDR (250 ms + RTT + encode + IDR transfer, over a second on 1 Mbit/s). airhand drains moderate backlogs and resets only beyond 8 queued in the decoder or 120 frames (client/src/lib/video.ts:34-35, 108-112, 171); its cap probes 15%/s far from capacity and 4%/s near it.

All in viewer/sink.rs and viewer/fps_cap.rs:
1. Signals per 250 ms tick: pulls (units take() handed out); backlogged tick (queue non-empty at both ends, no restart or drop between); measured capacity = pulls in backlogged ticks over their time across the last 8 ticks, valid once >= 4 backlogged ticks (1 s); head wait (age of the queue head); consumer lag: record presented_at - handed_at (sink.rs:704-741) in a 128-slot ring, excess = median over the last 1 s minus minimum over the last 10 s (near 0 on Darwin and Windows; grows by a decode time per hidden unit on a saturated Linux pipeline).
2. Lowering: today's triggers (a drop or backlog episode, or more than 2 queued on two ticks) plus excess consumer lag over max(2/cap s, 40 ms) on two ticks. capacity = the measured capacity when valid, else presented_fps; cap = floor(capacity x 0.9 direct or 0.8 relayed), at least CAP_MIN; the halving bound applies only when capacity came from presented_fps. Remember capacity and when.
3. Raising: with no known capacity, or up to hold = floor(0.95 x capacity): 3 s hold then one change a second, step = max(CAP_STEP x max(1, round(ceiling / 30)), ceil(0.25 x cap)) (R10's ceiling scaling: 20 at 120, 10 at 60, 5 at 30, merged with R5's 25% step). Above hold a raise is a probe: step max(1, ceil(0.1 x capacity)), allowed only after probe_backoff since the last failed probe (3 s doubling to 60 s, reset by a successful probe).
4. Probe watch (3 s after a probe): one tick with (>= 2 queued and head wait > max(2/cap s, 40 ms)) or excess consumer lag above the same reverts at once to the pre-probe cap (exempt from CAP_CHANGE_MIN) and doubles probe_backoff; a probe that survives forgets capacity and resets the backoff.
5. Forget capacity on a new generation, a picture-size change or a preset change.
6. Age backlog drains (R5-drain-age-backlog): on age, at push or take, when no age episode is open: open one, request the IDR through Recovery as today (KeyframeReason::Backlog; limiter and backoff unchanged, so the request time is unchanged), count it in backlog_drops (its meaning becomes 'backlog episodes'), tell the fps cap once, and do NOT clear the queue or set wait_key; keep enqueueing. The episode closes when an IDR is pushed (which already supersedes the queue with discontinuity, sink.rs:377-394) or the head's age falls below BACKLOG_AGE/2. Overflow (32 units, 8 MiB) still drops to the next IDR exactly as today. Recovery is unchanged (the awaited-IDR episode ends only when the IDR or a later frame is presented); the stall watchdog is unchanged.
7. Unchanged: CAP_MIN, the factors, the ceiling and its removal (sending max_fps), freeze() and the 500 ms IDR_GRACE judging.
8. Docs: 'Viewer: newest decodable frame, fps cap and recovery' and the sink module doc; CHANGELOG bullet with measured figures.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (deterministic fps_cap and sink tests with synthetic Instants: today's sequence far from capacity; the ceiling-scaled step (60 -> 120 within the 3 s hold plus 3 changes); probe backoff and the revert exempt from CAP_CHANGE_MIN; a transient low capacity recovers within one backoff; the consumer-lag trigger; an age backlog keeps the queue, requests one IDR per episode and notifies the cap once; the arriving IDR supersedes with discontinuity; overflow still drops; Recovery ends only on the IDR's presentation); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: On this Mac, release, 3 runs before and after: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 slow_link`. slow_presenter_is_capped_by_fps_cap_not_host_backpressure extended to 60 s: from 10 s on backlog_drops == 0, keyframes_requested == 0, mean_pace in [13, 15] (baseline slow_link.txt:12). New: slow_decoder_speeds_up (67 ms per unit for 20 s then 5 ms; seconds until the cap is removed, no slower than before, about 13 s); pipelined_slow_consumer (a 4-deep internal queue decoded at 67 ms per unit on a second thread; backlog_drops after 10 s must be 0, received-to-presented p95 from desktop_frame_view); fast_consumer_at_120 (10 ms decoder, fps_override 120; sink wait p95 and drops unchanged or better); a 120 fps LAN session with 1 s of injected backlog (time until received fps >= 115); consumer_stall_drains (a 2 ms decoder stalls once for 400 ms at 10 s, on TYPICAL and on 1 Mbit/s: time from the stall's end to the first presentation of a unit received after it began, present_interval max, keyframes_requested, backlog_drops). Every other slow_link case passes unchanged (lan_rtt_keeps_60, encoder_latency_of_45ms_keeps_60, idr_slower_than_a_second_is_followed_not_replaced and requested_idr_on_a_slow_link with no new keyframe requests). Record under docs/benchmarks/. Device: real Linux GStreamer software decode (1080p120 on a weak CPU), Windows software MF in a VM, 4K120 on an iGPU, and real decoder stalls.
verifiable_here: Measure-on-this-Mac (sink logic and slow_link with test decoders); real decoders are device-only.

name: linux-gpu-convert
title: Linux viewer: keep decoded pictures on the GPU, converted in Flutter's GL context through an FlTextureGL (module ABI 2, dma-buf where available)
protocol_changes: None on the wire or the FFI. The runner-module C ABI goes from 1 to 2 (bump PB_VIDEO_MODULE_ABI to one above master's value at merge); both are built together and the ABI check (desktop_video.cc:109) rejects a stale module. File and symbol names stay.
design:
Why. Today every hardware-decoded picture is downloaded to system memory (NV12: 3.1 MB at 1080p, 12.4 MB at 4K), converted to RGBA on the CPU by up to 4 videoconvert threads (desktop_video_gst.cc:88, 575-579), and re-specified into Flutter's texture as RGBA (8.3 or 33 MB). Estimated saving: 4-12 ms of CPU per 1080p picture and 15-40 ms per 4K picture across threads, which matters for laptop battery and thermals and makes 1440p or 4K at 60+ possible on iGPU laptops. Merged duplicate: R10-linux-gpu-convert (same goal; it also notes Flutter's Linux embedder takes at most 60 frames a second, so at 120 fps half of today's CPU conversions are discarded).

Design (the corrected one: no GstGL on the default path, the module stays GL-free and hands over the decoder's native picture; the runner converts in whatever GL context presents it, so no context bootstrap, no cross-context sync and no new runtime package):
1. Measurement commit first: module stats gain `timings.decode`; the harness prints CPU ms per decoded picture per thread from getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD).
2. Module ABI 2 (desktop_video_module.h:79-111): pipeline appsrc -> parse -> decoder -> appsink with no videoconvert; appsink caps video/x-raw,format={NV12,I420}; add video/x-raw(memory:DMABuf),format=DMA_DRM,drm-format=<NV12 with the modifiers the presenter imports> only when the presenter reports dma-buf import and GStreamer >= 1.24; a decoder that offers none of these gets videoconvert to NV12. Candidates (166-223) accept decoders whose source pad offers system memory or DMABuf. create takes the presenter's capabilities (dma-buf import yes/no, modifier list). New describe(picture, PbVideoPlanes*) gives visible width/height and format, colour matrix and range from the caps (DefaultColorimetry keeps its BT.709 default), and per plane either {data, stride} or {dmabuf fd, offset, stride, drm fourcc, modifier}, using GstVideoMeta offsets so 1088-row surfaces crop. `pixels` is replaced by snapshot(picture, max_width, rgba out), which for system memory uses a GstVideoConverter scaling straight to <= 320 px. The module links gstreamer-allocators-1.0 (in libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev).
3. Runner GL helper, new ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_gl.cc (epoxy, which libgtk-3-dev brings): plane textures R8/RG8, or LUMINANCE/LUMINANCE_ALPHA on ES2 without EXT_texture_rg, updated with glTexSubImage2D (GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH where available, else padded rows with scaled texture coordinates); or per-plane EGLImages (eglCreateImageKHR(EGL_LINUX_DMA_BUF_EXT, DRM_FORMAT_R8/GR88, modifier), cached per pooled buffer, glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES). One shader pass (BT.709 or BT.601, limited or full range, from describe) into an RGBA8 GL_TEXTURE_2D through an FBO, saving and restoring every GL binding it touches as fl_compositor_opengl.cc:222-245, 348-358 do. An EGL fence after the pass; a picture returns to GStreamer only once its fence signalled (checked without waiting at the next call); hold at most 2 pictures. Capabilities read on the GTK thread at create without a context: eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT on GDK's native display (the EGLDisplay fl_opengl_manager.cc:47-61 obtains; initialize if needed, never eglTerminate), EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import(_modifiers), eglQueryDmaBufModifiersEXT for NV12; GL_OES_EGL_image confirmed at the first conversion, else the runner tells the module, which falls back to system memory at the next keyframe and asks for one once.
4. PbVideoTexture becomes an FlTextureGL subclass (desktop_video.cc:228-303): populate acquires the newest picture (the receipt), converts it and returns GL_TEXTURE_2D/GL_RGBA8 (suits Skia and Impeller); before the first picture a 1x1 black texture. For dma-buf pictures the helper refreshes an RGBA readback of <= 320 px at most once a second for snapshot. FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software keeps today's path.
5. Optional NVIDIA stage (NVDEC GLMemory through CUDA-GL interop) only if device numbers show NVDEC's download plus YUV upload still costs more than about 2 ms per 4K picture.
6. Build and CI: runner/CMakeLists.txt links epoxy; the module adds gstreamer-allocators-1.0; syntax-check.yml linux-app adds libegl1, libegl-mesa0 and libgles2 for the harness. No new runtime package in the user guide (no gstreamer1.0-gl).
7. Harness (ui/linux/test/desktop_video_test.cc:104-200): a surfaceless EGL ES2 context (llvmpipe) stands in for the raster thread and calls the helper; checks the converted texture is GL_TEXTURE_2D RGBA8 of the picture's size, glReadPixels of the converted test pattern matches videoconvert's RGBA of the same picture at PSNR >= 40 dB (BT.709 limited), the snapshot is non-uniform, and the software (libav I420) path decodes with no videoconvert.
8. Docs: 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (remote-desktop.md:2204-2266); CHANGELOG bullet with device figures.
verification: Here, from ui/: `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (no Dart change expected). CI linux-app (ubuntu-22.04): `flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software` (GL helper correctness on llvmpipe: format, size, PSNR against videoconvert; decoded/s and presented/s for the 720p and 1080p clips before and after; CI CPU figures on llvmpipe are not gains).
measurement: Device-only, before and after: Intel iGPU with iHD on Ubuntu 24.04 (GStreamer 1.24) under GNOME Wayland and GNOME X11; AMD with radeonsi VA; NVIDIA with NVDEC on X11. The harness in hardware mode at 1080p and 4K offered at 60 and 120 fps: decoded/s, presented/s, CPU ms per picture per thread; the app at 1080p60 and 4K60: `pidstat -t -p <pid> 1`, stats timings decode and surface_consume, intel_gpu_top / radeontop / `nvidia-smi dmon`. Confirm on 1.24 that dma-buf was negotiated (G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=pb-mapper-video logs the caps) and on a 1.22 distro that it was not. Record under docs/benchmarks/ with the environment.
verifiable_here: Device-only for the effect; CI builds the runner and runs the llvmpipe correctness harness. Nothing Linux runs on this Mac.

name: direct-cooldown
title: Share the direct-fallback cooldown across connect_tcp calls per Client and service
design:
Why. CLAUDE.md's invariant says that after a pre-commit fallback the consumer pauses direct (10 s doubling to 5 min), so an unpunchable path costs one attempt, not one per connection. Today the cooldown lives in each Consumer, and every connect_tcp (each viewer session and reconnect) builds a new one, so every reconnect behind a symmetric NAT or blocked UDP pays about 2-3 s of punch setup again; the app's reconnect backoff of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 s (desktop_store.dart:22) falls inside the cooldown.

1. ClientInner (sdk/client.rs:36) gets `direct_memory: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<DirectMemory>>`: at most 64 entries, evicting expired ones first, keyed by (relay endpoint identity, namespace, service key); each entry holds the Cooldown, the TCP Cooldown and the network generation of its last back-off.
2. run_owned_stream (client/mod.rs:408) passes the entry into Consumer::new; cooldown() and tcp_cooldown() read through it and report it cleared when the generation differs. A direct success clears it, as today; diagnostics.direct_cooldown is reported as today.
3. Listener workers are unchanged (they already share one Consumer).
4. Step 2, sharing the consumer Network (UDP sockets, STUN result, port-mapping lease) per entry with a 60 s idle expiry, only if the existing SetupTimings diagnostics show discovery plus mapping of at least 100 ms per connect on devices.
5. Docs: the direct fallback paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-client --all-features --lib direct::` (with crate::test_relay::TestRelay, since pb-mapper-client cannot use the testkit, and a cfg(test) fault that makes the punch fail: two consecutive connect_tcp calls, the second shows cooldown_skip and its time to first byte falls by at least PUNCH_BUDGET; a bumped network generation clears the entry); `cargo test -p pb-mapper-cli --all-features --test e2e direct`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux: `cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`.
measurement: Time to first byte of a second connect_tcp inside the cooldown, printed in a release run before (master) and after. Device: a viewer behind a symmetric NAT reconnecting: time to first picture per reconnect.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test and the time-to-first-byte comparison here; real NATs device-only (CI's nat-traversal gate covers the invariants).

name: relay-tcp-tuning
title: Linux relay: disable TCP slow start after idle (Docker sysctl, opt-in install step, startup notice) and opt-in BBR on relay sockets
protocol_changes: None on the wire. Relay server option `--tcp-congestion <name>` (env PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION, read at startup only), off by default, added to RelayServerOptions following its existing pattern without breaking public struct literals.
design:
Why. (a) Linux restarts a TCP connection's congestion window from IW10 after an idle period (net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle = 1), so on relayed sessions the first scroll, window switch or IDR after a still period slow-starts: an estimated 100-400 ms more latency on that first burst over 50-150 ms legs. (b) With Cubic the relay->viewer leg's throughput ceiling is about 1.2 x MSS / (RTT x sqrt(p)): roughly 0.9 Mbit/s at 1% loss and 150 ms, below every preset's rate, so pace and bpf collapse on lossy cross-border and cellular legs; kernel BBR (mature BBRv1/v3 with a decaying bandwidth filter) is not limited by random loss.

1. docker/docker-compose.yml: `sysctls: net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle: 0` with a comment that it needs Linux 4.15+ and is namespaced to the container; a commented line for the congestion option.
2. scripts/install-server-github.sh and -gitee.sh: an opt-in prompt that writes /etc/sysctl.d/90-pb-mapper.conf.
3. pb-mapper-server on Linux, at startup: read /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_slow_start_after_idle; when 1, log one info event relay_tcp_idle_restart naming the fix (read-only).
4. `--tcp-congestion <name>`: on each accepted relay socket (connection.rs:117-121) set TCP_CONGESTION best effort (socket2's set_tcp_congestion); on EPERM or ENOENT log once with the fix (modprobe tcp_bbr plus net.ipv4.tcp_allowed_congestion_control, or CAP_NET_ADMIN in Docker). Only the relay's sending direction changes, which carries the relay->viewer video leg. Opt-in keeps zero cost by default; the fairness trade-off is the operator's choice.
5. Docs: an operator note in the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) and DOCKER_README.md; CHANGELOG without figures.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (option parsing; the sysctl reader as a pure function over file content); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux (`cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`), node-e2e (CLI flags still parse).
measurement: Device only, on a Linux relay (VM or the ubuntu CI runner with sudo): `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 50ms` with the relay on loopback; a testkit host and viewer (or transport_probe) idle 3 s, then ask for a keyframe (KeyframeReason::User): request-to-IDR-arrival time and cwnd from `ss -ti`, 20 rounds each at sysctl 1 and 0. BBR: `tc qdisc add dev <egress> root netem delay 75ms loss 0.1%` and `1%`, transport_probe and a desktop session through the relay, Cubic against BBR, 10 runs each: delivered Mbit/s, pace, sent_bitrate, IDR wait. Record under docs/benchmarks/<date>-relay-tcp/.
verifiable_here: Build and unit tests here; every effect is Linux-device-only.
